# Questions for the client (Wife)

These are refinements, not blockers — the deliverables are complete on stated assumptions. Answers will sharpen the advice.

1. **Refinance qualification.** Has any lender given you a pre-approval estimate on refinancing the $400,000 mortgage into your own name (income $72,000 + $2,000/mo maintenance + child support)? If you know your credit score or have quotes (rate/terms), the house plan's affordability can be confirmed instead of flagged as an assumption. (Lender underwriting is not something the reference library covers, so today it is unverified.)
2. **Prior-year bonuses.** Do you know whether Husband received bonuses in 2024 and 2025, and roughly how much? The 2026 documents establish the 2026 bonus ($45,000 target, 112% of plan); if bonuses are recurring, the guideline income finding gets stronger and any undisclosed-land "sanction" analysis widens.
3. **The September bonus money.** The 2026-09-15 stub shows $27,212 of YTD beyond salary (a September bonus installment of $22,500–$25,200 fits). Do you know whether the joint checking/savings balance (schedule says $100,000) includes that money, or whether Husband holds a separate account? If you can, check recent statements for a deposit of roughly $22.5k–$25.2k in September 2026.
4. **Your other debts and expenses.** For the refinance/budget picture: car loan or student loan balances and payments, your monthly ordinary spending, and any funds of yours outside the marital accounts.
5. **Wife's IRA / retirement.** Do you have an IRA or 401(k) of your own? It isn't on the schedule; if it exists and is marital or your separate property, it affects both the division math and your backup liquidity plan.
6. **Withdrawal plan for any 401(k) share you might take.** If the equalization is funded partly from his 401(k) by QDRO, would you want it rolled to an IRA (tax-deferred) rather than cashed out? No rate for your own bracket is in our reference library, so we'd flag the value either way — your decision only.
7. **Timing of the decree.** Is a final decree expected on or before December 31, 2026? It drives filing status (single/head-of-household in 2026) and the joint-sale option's availability.
